chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Abd Allah ibn Bahr, from Hariz ibn 'Abd Allah, who said:
It was said to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: “May the junub apply oil and then perform ghusl?” He said: “No.”
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is to be understood as indicating a kind of karahah, as shown by the reports we have previously presented.

key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: Narrations or reports used as supporting evidence.
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: A person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl.
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: Dislikedness; an act considered makruh rather than forbidden.
key_terms.يَدَّهِنُ: Applies oil or ointment to the body.

ai.seo_question: Is it disliked for a junub to apply oil before performing ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on a junub applying oil before performing ghusl. The Imam عليه السلام answers in the negative, and Shaykh al-Tusi explains that the report indicates karahah rather than absolute prohibition based on other narrations.
